cover: What software maintenance covers after launch

slides.title: Launch is when the upkeep starts
slides.body: Security updates, platform changes, monitoring and small fixes keep the product doing what it did on day one.

slides.title: Every integration is a moving part
slides.body: Each payment provider, plugin or outside API can change underneath you. More of them means more upkeep.

slides.title: Tests make every later change cheaper
slides.body: With automated tests and a staging site, each update gets checked before it goes live, not tested by hand.

slides.title: Sensitive data can't wait a month
slides.body: Health records or payment details need faster patching and access reviews, so the plan must allow urgent work.

slides.title: Neglect costs the most
slides.body: Two years without updates usually means a catch-up project, sometimes a framework upgrade, before routine work starts.

slides.title: Budget for it before the build ends
slides.body: Ask what depends on outside services while your developer still knows the whole system, then set a monthly line.
